items.question: What order are the rows in?
items.chose: Sorts rows by creation time ascending (oldest first), then by id as a string comparison, on a copy of the input.
items.instead: Keep the caller's input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has an unknown status?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id and the status, and the whole export fails.
items.instead: Write the raw status through, or skip the row.

items.question: What happens when openings or filled is negative, fractional, NaN, infinite or not a number?
items.chose: Throws an Error for the first invalid requisition, and the whole export fails.
items.instead: Skip the row, or coerce or clamp the value.

items.question: What happens when filled is greater than openings?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id.
items.instead: Export the numbers as they are, or clamp filled to openings.

items.question: What happens when createdAt is not a valid Date?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id.
items.instead: Write an empty date field, or skip the row.

items.question: Does one bad requisition fail the whole export or just that row?
items.chose: Validates every requisition before building any output, so one bad record throws and no CSV is returned.
items.instead: Skip the bad rows and export the rest, or collect all errors and report them together.

items.question: How are dates formatted in the Created column?
items.chose: Writes the full ISO 8601 UTC timestamp with milliseconds.
items.instead: Write a date only (YYYY-MM-DD), or use a locale or local-timezone format.

items.question: What are the column names and their order?
items.chose: Uses the header 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created' with fixed English labels.
items.instead: Use the field names (id,title,status,openings,filled,createdAt), or add other columns such as an open count.

items.question: Does the output start with a UTF-8 byte order mark?
items.chose: Prepends a BOM (U+FEFF) to the output.
items.instead: Return plain CSV text with no BOM.

items.question: Which line terminator is used, and does the output end with one?
items.chose: Ends every line, including the last, with CRLF.
items.instead: Use LF only, or join lines with no trailing newline.

items.question: How is an empty requisition list exported?
items.chose: Returns the BOM and header line only, with no error.
items.instead: Return an empty string, or throw.

items.question: How are missing or null titles, and fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks, handled?
items.chose: Writes a null or undefined title as an empty field. Quotes fields containing a comma, quote, CR or LF per RFC 4180. Does not guard against spreadsheet formula injection.
items.instead: Write the string 'null', or also prefix values starting with =, +, - or @ to neutralise formulas.
